p: Renting a motorbike in Hanoi is one of the most practical ways to explore the city and its surroundings. Our rental shop in Long Bien offers semi-automatic bikes, automatic scooters, 50cc motorbikes and electric motorbikes with daily, weekly and monthly rental options.

This hub is the starting point of our Hanoi motorbike rental guide library. From here you can reach every topic: rental prices, scooters, 50cc bikes, areas like the Old Quarter, monthly hire and motorbike trips out of the city.

s.h: Why rent a motorbike in Hanoi
p: Hanoi is a city built for two wheels. Distances between the Old Quarter, Hoan Kiem, Tay Ho, Cau Giay and Long Bien are short, traffic moves at low speeds, and parking a motorbike is far easier than finding space for a car.

For visitors, a rental motorbike means freedom from ride-hailing waits and fixed tour schedules. For expats, it is the everyday commuting default. Both start with the same question: which bike, for how long, at what verified price.

Our lineup covers the common rental categories in Hanoi. Semi-automatic bikes such as the Honda Wave and Yamaha Sirius are simple, tough and cheap to run. Automatic scooters such as the Honda Vision, Honda Click, Honda Air Blade and Yamaha Mio are the easiest to ride in stop-and-go traffic.

We also rent 50cc motorbikes for riders who want the lightest possible machine, and electric motorbikes for quiet, low-emission city travel. Availability changes — always contact us to confirm the bike you want for your dates.

50cc Motorbike Rental in Hanoi

A 50cc motorbike or scooter is the lightest, easiest way to move around Hanoi. With a small engine and simple controls, 50cc bikes suit riders who want a low-effort city machine for short hops and slow streets.
Our verified 50cc rate is 200,000 VND/day. We do not publish weekly or monthly 50cc prices because they are not verified — contact us directly for a quote for longer periods.

A 50cc moped is best for calm, flat, city-centre riding: Hoan Kiem, the Old Quarter, the French Quarter and lakeside loops. It is not built for long distances, highways or mountain routes — for those, a 110cc+ semi-automatic or a proper scooter is the better tool.
Because 50cc bikes are small and light, they are easier to push into tight parking spots and simpler for less experienced riders to handle at low speed.
The verified price for a 50cc scooter or motorbike is 200,000 VND/day. For weekly or monthly 50cc rental we quote individually — we will not invent rates we have not verified.

Motorbike Rental Hanoi Old Quarter

The Old Quarter is the heart of Hanoi for most visitors — narrow streets, dense traffic and very limited parking. Renting a motorbike gives you freedom in and around the Old Quarter, but riding and parking there take some know-how.
Our shop is located in Long Bien, a short ride from the Old Quarter. This hub covers renting near the Old Quarter, parking realities, and how to move between central Hanoi areas on two wheels.
Old Quarter streets are narrow, often one-way and always busy. Speeds are low, which is good news for riders: the rhythm of the area is stop-and-go, and a light automatic scooter handles it best.
Weekends bring pedestrian zones around Hoan Kiem Lake, when some streets close to traffic. Plan around them — they are pleasant to walk, not to ride.

Sidewalk parking attendants are the norm. You pay a small fee, take a ticket and leave your bike in a marked row. Never assume parking is free or that a spot is legal — follow the attendants and the crowd.

From Long Bien, the ride to the Old Quarter crosses the Red River side of the city and takes roughly twenty to thirty minutes depending on traffic. Our staff can point you to the simplest route for your first ride.

p: Hanoi Motorbike Trips & Routes

Hanoi is an excellent base for motorbike travel. Within a day ride you can reach the limestone landscapes of Ninh Binh, the mountains of Ba Vi, the highland valley of Mai Chau or the ancient houses of Duong Lam.
This hub gathers route ideas, distances and planning tips for motorbike trips from Hanoi — from half-day escapes to longer loops through Northern Vietnam.
Popular directions out of the city

s.h: Popular directions out of the city
p: South: Ninh Binh, roughly 100 km from Hanoi, with karst scenery, rivers and temples — the classic full-day ride. West: Ba Vi National Park for mountain roads, and Duong Lam ancient village for a shorter half-day loop. Further west: Mai Chau, best as an overnight trip.
Each direction mixes highway stretches with rural roads. Plan fuel stops in towns, start early to beat city traffic, and check your rental bike before a long day — brakes, tyres, fuel and lights.

s.h: Choosing a bike for a trip
p: For long day trips, comfort matters more than in city riding. Semi-automatics like the Honda Wave and Yamaha Sirius are simple and economical; scooters like the Honda Vision and Air Blade are more comfortable at higher speeds. A 50cc bike is a city machine and not suited to intercity routes.
Contact us about which model fits your route and your riding experience, and to confirm availability for your travel dates.

p: Hanoi Motorbike for Sale: Buying vs Renting

If you are staying in Hanoi long enough, the buying-versus-renting question comes up quickly. Buying a used motorbike involves purchase price, ownership paperwork, insurance, maintenance and the hassle of reselling it when you leave.
This guide is informational — we are a rental service, not a motorbike dealer. We lay out the real cost and effort on both sides so you can decide whether buying or renting suits your stay.

Beyond the sticker price of a used bike, ownership adds registration and paperwork (more involved for foreigners), insurance, repairs and maintenance, and the time cost of selling the bike before you leave — often at a loss and always at short notice.
Old used bikes sold cheaply to travelers often need work: tyres, brakes, batteries and carburetors are the usual suspects. A low purchase price rarely stays low.

Renting wins on simplicity for stays under a few months: no paperwork in your name, no maintenance responsibility, and verified rates that are easy to budget. Our monthly ranges start at 900,000 VND, which keeps long-stay rental competitive with ownership once repair risk is priced in.
Renting also lets you match the bike to the ride — a scooter for the city, a semi-automatic for a trip — instead of owning one compromise machine.

p: Renting a Motorbike in Vietnam

Renting a motorbike in Vietnam is a highlight of many trips — and it works best when you understand the rules and practices before you ride. This guide covers the essentials: what documents matter, how rental shops operate, and what to check before accepting a bike.

License and legal requirements depend on your home country, your length of stay and the bike you ride. We do not give legal advice — always confirm current requirements with official sources and your rental shop.
How rental shops in Vietnam work

s.h: How rental shops in Vietnam work
p: The typical pattern: you choose a bike, agree on a rate and a period, leave identification or a deposit as the shop requires, sign a simple contract, and take the bike. Read what you sign and photograph the bike’s condition before you ride away.
Reputable shops publish real prices, tell you what is and is not included, and answer availability questions honestly. That is the standard we hold ourselves to.

Check brakes, tyres, lights, horn, fuel level and the general state of the machine. Confirm the return time and place, what happens in case of breakdown or damage, and who to call. Small questions before the ride prevent big problems during it.
If anything feels wrong with the bike, ask for a different one. Availability varies — which is exactly why we confirm every booking by phone or email rather than promising models in advance.

Motorbike Guides: Safety, Parking, Fuel & Maintenance

Riding in Hanoi rewards preparation. Our guides cover the everyday knowledge that keeps a rental ride smooth: how to park legally, where to fill fuel, how to handle Hanoi traffic patterns and what basic checks to do on a rental bike.
These guides are written for visitors and expats renting motorbikes in Hanoi, with neutral, factual information and no invented promises.

Hanoi traffic flows like water — vehicles merge, weave and filter constantly. The safe response is predictability: steady speed, clear signals, no sudden moves, and eyes always scanning a few vehicles ahead.
Right of way in practice is negotiated by position and speed rather than strict rules. Ride defensively, assume you are less visible than you think, and keep to the right on larger roads.

Fuel: petrol stations are common in Hanoi; know which side your tank opens before you arrive at the pump. Parking: use attended parking lots and sidewalk rows, keep the ticket, and never block shop fronts. Rain: in the wet season, expect sudden downpours — pull over and wait rather than ride through the first ten minutes, which are the most slippery.
Maintenance on a rental is our responsibility, not yours — but a daily walk-around (tyres, brakes, lights, fuel) keeps small issues from ending a ride.
